title: Crystal Palace to play AEK Larnaca in Conference League round of 16
content:
Crystal Palace have been drawn against Cypriot club AEK Larnaca in the Conference League round of 16.

Palace, playing their first ever European campaign, earned a spot in the last-16 after defeating Zrinjski Mostar 3-1 on aggregate in the play-off round.

Oliver Glasner’s side drew 1-1 with the nine-time champions of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the first leg, but goals from Maxence Lacroix and Evann Guessand gave Palace a 2-0 win in the second leg at Selhurst Park on Thursday.

Palace are already familiar with AEK, having been defeated at home by the team from Cyprus in this season’s league phase. Riad Bajic scored the only goal of the game after a mistake from 19-year-old Palace defender Jaydee Canvot, who gave the ball away inside his own half.

Palace had 67 per cent possession in the game and had 16 shots, though just one was on target.

AEK are third in the Cypriot First Division, eight points behind leaders Omonoia Nicosia. They won three and drew three of their league phase games and conceded only one goal.

Palace will play the first leg at home on March 12, with the return leg being played seven days later at the AEK Arena in Cyprus.

If Palace are victorious, they will play either Italy’s Fiorentina or Polish side Rakow Czestochowa in the quarter-finals.

The south London club were forced to go through the play-off round after finishing outside the top eight in the league phase, winning three games, drawing one and losing two.

Palace have won just three of their last 17 games in all competitions with speculation over Glasner’s future. The Austrian manager has confirmed that he will leave the club when his contract expires this summer, but has not ruled out departing before that stage.

Tensions between Glasner — who won the FA Cup with Palace last season, their first major trophy — and the club’s fans have risen in recent weeks, with Glasner saying that the fans needed to “stay humble”. In response, a banner was unfurled by the Holmesdale Fanatics during the 1-0 win over Wolverhampton Wanderers which said that the manager was “finished”.

Palace are 13th in the Premier League and visit fourth-placed Manchester United on Sunday.
